comparator.sourceNotes: Freshly retrieved 2026–2027 EEMCS OER, articles 6–7 (PDF pp.25–29), controls the ordinary current requirements. Year one has twelve required 5-EC courses. Year two has nine required 5-EC courses, Electrical Engineering for the Next Generation 10 EC and one restricted elective 5 EC. Year three has a genuine approved minor 30 EC, Signal Processing 5 EC, Computer Architecture and Organisation 5 EC, a second restricted elective 5 EC and the graduation project 15 EC. Year totals are 60+60+60=180. Select the first two distinct listed options, EEX01 Introduction to Machine Learning in year two and EEX02 Communication Networks and Algorithms in year three, independently of UCR fit; EEX03–05 are unselected alternatives, not extra credits. Minor content must not overlap the selected electives. The formal table places Mixed-Signal Circuits and Systems EE2C2 in Q3 while the still-linked 2025–2026 chart puts it in Q4; exact quarter scheduling is not asserted or derived from an assumed 15-EC quarterly allocation. Current formal entry requirements replace older chart statements: Project 1 requires the Linear Circuits A course lab and Introduction mentorship; Project 2 requires Project 1 and both Digital Systems labs; Project 3 requires positive BSA, Project 1, Signals and Systems lab and either Linear Circuits B or Calculus. Electives require positive BSA; Next Generation requires all three projects and Electrical Energy Fundamentals or Linear Algebra and Differential Equations, with at least 5 in the other. Graduation requires every first- and second-year course. Dutch admission proficiency remains distinct from the predominantly English course instruction and mixed English/Dutch first-year projects. The module-level weights and yearly allocation are verified; no precise external timetable is certified. Current tables and choice/prerequisite clauses visually inspected on 8 October 2026. UCR assessment on 10 October 2026 freshly retrieved the controlling adopted OER and visually inspected its current programme table. All corrected components, restricted choices, genuine minor space and graduation prerequisites remain unchanged. The older module chart does not override the current regulation.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Workbook checks passed: 24 unique courses, 180 EC, PPD in year one, at least six advanced courses, all recorded prerequisites in earlier semesters and exact Fall 2026 cohort availability. Networks is placed in its sole semester three; numerical methods, linear systems, advanced algorithms and robotics occupy the four sole-semester-four places. Programming/discrete foundations and introductory mathematics precede advanced algorithms and systems. Optimisation follows programming; it is permitted alongside introductory mathematics under the recorded prerequisite. Energy foundations precede renewable-energy assessment; brain foundations and introductory neuroscience precede advanced neurophysiology. Software Development cannot also fit semester four, and the unavailable Energy & Sustainability course was not used.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two complete and substantively distinct related-fields curricula are feasible. Energy/transport electrification, communication and autonomous methods are already substantively owned by the closest concept; the medical-electronics direction leads to a genuine biological-signal alternative. A third circuit/chip/electromagnetic-device programme cannot obtain its defining content or experimental design progression from this workbook. AI/software study does not supply semiconductor devices, electronic construction or electromagnetic engineering. No unavailable course or arbitrary third direction is introduced.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both provide calculus foundations; the UCR gateway also introduces linear algebra. This is a substantive partial relationship, not equal-credit syllabus equivalence.
The UCR course develops the linear-algebra part through systems, matrices and vector spaces; the external component also includes calculus.
Advanced calculus includes differential equations and complex functions, addressing the differential-equation part; linear algebra is studied elsewhere and is not double-aligned.
The UCR course directly analyses linear systems with transfer functions, state-space and signal-flow methods and documented signal/control applications.
Both provide probability and mathematical statistics for quantitative modelling and measurement uncertainty.
The UCR course directly studies computer communication networks and their operation. It does not cover all communication-network algorithms or transmission physics.
Both introduce machine-learning models and their implementation; the external restricted choice remains the independently selected first-listed option.

No sufficiently supported primary subject/method counterpart is asserted. The entire external component remains visible and credited once; related mathematical or computational courses do not supply its complete electrical subject.
